summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development, made a new worktree (parallel-join), joined the existing ledger and ran `verify`. It then tried `sdd-state claim` on tasks 1 and 2 and got `status=held` for both. It asked whether to take over, I said no, and it handed back without using --takeover. But it never ran `sdd-state next`, `sdd-state wait ... --kind tasks` or `sdd-state board`, and no waiting/ file exists. Instead it noted that it was waiting by appending a free-text line to progress.md. The empty-frontier rule this story tests was not followed.
reasoning: Criteria 2, 3 and 4 failed: the session log has no sdd-state next/wait/board call and no waiting/ file exists on disk. Criteria 1, 5 and 6 passed. The loaded skill seems to lack these verbs, which suggests the control plugin build was used rather than the candidate.

observations.description: The plugin under test (hp-control) does not seem to have the empty-frontier protocol. Running `grep -E 'sdd-state (next|wait|board)|kind tasks'` on skills/subagent-driven-development/*.md returned nothing, and scripts/sdd-state has no next/wait/board case labels. So the agent could not have followed the rule. Either the wrong candidate plugin was loaded (--plugin-dir points at .../parallel-development/hp-control, which looks like a control build) or the feature is missing.

The agent's first claim commands used "$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID" and were blocked by a worktree-isolation guard: "this command runs sdd-state with a value computed at runtime ... inside a construct too complex to verify". It retried with the literal session id. That wasted turns.
The waiting state was recorded only as a free-text line in progress.md, not as a structured waiting record. Other sessions can't easily find or act on it.

During Claude Code startup, the trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs both default to 'No, exit'. A 'Newer Opus model available' prompt also appeared even though --model claude-opus-5-5 was passed, and it said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5'.
The agent made a worktree (branch worktree-parallel-join) even though it could do no work. It did offer to remove it in its hand-back message.

criteria.criterion: Invoked subagent-driven-development skill before any other work
Ran `sdd-state next` and output shows `none reason=held`
criteria.evidence: List of Bash commands from the session log: the sdd-state verbs used were sync, verify and claim (x2), plus retries. There was no `next`. `grep -c -E 'sdd-state (next|wait|board)'` on the jsonl returned 0. Held status came from claim instead: "status=held task=1 owner=fixture-session ... Exit code 4"

criteria.criterion: Posted waiting record of kind tasks; a file under waiting/ holds kind=tasks
criteria.evidence: No `sdd-state wait` in the transcript (same grep returned 0). `find .cache -path '*waiting*'` under the harness home returned nothing. The agent instead appended this to progress.md: "session 2bea309a-...: tasks 1,2 held by fixture-session; user declined takeover (other session still working); idle, awaiting instruction"
`grep -o 'sdd-state [a-z]*'` across the transcript found claim, finish, handoff, prune, snapshot, sync, verify and with, but no board. None of the agent's Bash commands ran board.

criteria.criterion: Handed back saying every task is held by another session
criteria.evidence: Final message on screen: "I've joined the plan from a new worktree, but this session can't run either task: your other session holds both claims, and you said it's still working." After that the prompt was idle.

criteria.criterion: Did not take over a held task (no Bash command with --takeover)
criteria.evidence: Every Bash input pulled from the jsonl with jq: none contains --takeover. The string appears only in the AskUserQuestion option descriptions and in the loaded skill text. The user answered "No, the other session is still working."
